acceptanceCriteria: Reproduce the same-owner closed-session/live-replacement case with genuine isolated pipeline sessions and active claims; assert current behavior cannot silently count reanchored success as restored authority.

Provide a supported atomic same-owner recovery that validates the unique live replacement runtime, role, agent and generation before rebinding, or explicitly refuses with a correct supported recovery instruction instead of refreshing the lease while retaining dead authority. Never reopen the closed SID or edit claim metadata outside the owning native writer.

Cover open-session no-op, closed predecessor with one valid replacement, absent or ambiguous replacement, wrong role/runtime/agent/generation, phase or owner CAS races, and concurrent session closure; preserve normal foreign reclaim fences, legitimate review-repair rules, and historical receipt provenance.

Land the owning Core repair with required focused regressions, relevant full gate and independent review; retain exact version, original reproduction and acceptance evidence, then link genuine Core closure before completing this EXTERNAL Corvint intake. No Corvint source change or task-local glob fix is implied.
body:
Confirmed native Beamfall Core recovery gap, observed 2026-09-30 during PLUGIN-SDK-0-3-2-ADOPT-1. Implementation and closure owner: Beamfall Core, not Corvint Tasks. A task-local request/reply glob bug caused the original controller to exit and close its session; that separate task-local bug is explicitly NOT attributed to Corvint or this native defect. The native defect is that same-owner reclaim reports reanchored success but retains the now-closed pipeline_builder_session despite a genuine live replacement builder session for that same runtime/agent/generation.

Version/evidence: Core HEAD 5dead47f49f24f56e77c9901d5ff4f86bb2579a5; script/roadmap_pipeline.py SHA256 539cb40c79841beb3c40b67ed121bc75ab79e0f71643890f3481b66b0332fb6b. Corvint Tasks intake CLI 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build.202 (go1.27.1); not the defective runtime. Root observed original actual PID 85018 / session prefix 98bf7d40 closed, replacement actual PID 9818 / session prefix 6a3a open, while claim remained bound to the closed original. Session identifiers are intentionally recorded only as reported prefixes here; do not infer full UUIDs. Source investigation is read-only; no second production reproduction was attempted.

Reproduction: (1) In an isolated fixture, open an actual builder session A and claim an active ticket so it is receipt-bound to A. (2) Close A without completing its active ticket. (3) Open genuine session B with the same runtime and agent, current generation, and actual replacement PID. (4) Call supported roadmap.sh reclaim for that actor. (5) It reports reanchored:true and updates agent_pid/last_heartbeat, but pipeline_builder_session remains A. (6) validate_session(A) correctly rejects it as closed; opening/heartbeating B does not restore the claim binding. The reported live observation plus exact native branch confirms this behavior; retain a runnable isolated regression in the owning repair.

Source: script/roadmap_pipeline.py:943-948 returns early for owner == args.agent after only PID/heartbeat updates. validate_session at 308-324 rejects closed sessions. session-open 341-365 reuses only OPEN rows, creating a distinct UUID for a closed predecessor without changing existing claims. claim-commit 497-528 binds new claims only. review-repair 754-794 has a legitimate original-agent replacement branch, but only for needs_work plus canonical FAIL/recovery evidence and therefore is not an active-lane workaround. Foreign reclaim 951-984 enforces existing dead-PID 15-minute/crash-TTL fences and current-generation own-session selection before changing binding. Shell wrapper script/roadmap.sh:13917-13934 exposes no same-owner rebind option.

Current supported containment: close the replacement same-agent session, retire the owned controller normally, use a genuinely distinct resumed actor/session and the unchanged 15-minute foreign-owner fence; then native reclaim can rebind. This is recovery, not a durable fix. No SID revival, direct claim edits, fake failure transition, shortened fence, dummy owner or fabricated receipt is acceptable.

Dedup: native searches for reclaim, rebind, and closed session found no equivalent ticket. CORE-CLOSED-SESSION-KEEPER-RESPAWN-1 covers the separate fleet guard respawn defect and is not duplicated here. Core closure metadata: retain owning Core ticket/change, exact fixed commit/source version, isolated before/after reproduction, session/claim provenance checks, relevant owning gate and independent review evidence. Keep this external intake OPEN until Core fix integration and native completion evidence are linked; Corvint receipt consistency is not product closure or runtime qualification.
title: Core reclaim: same-owner recovery retains a closed builder session despite a live replacement
